subsystems.name: Mooring grid
subsystems.role: holds the whole farm in place and lets lines sit at chosen depths in the water column.

subsystems.name: Seaweed grow-out
subsystems.role: grows kelp on seeded lines suspended below the surface.
parts: seed twine wrapped around the line
floats to set the line depth

subsystems.name: Shellfish and bottom culture
subsystems.role: uses the layers beneath the seaweed for filter feeders and lower-trophic species.
parts: hanging cages or lantern nets for mussels, oysters, scallops

subsystems.name: Hatchery and seeding
subsystems.role: produces the juvenile seaweed and shellfish that the farm is stocked with.

subsystems.name: Harvest system
subsystems.role: gets the crop off the line quickly, before it degrades.

subsystems.name: Processing and cold chain
subsystems.role: turns wet biomass into something storable and saleable.

buildSteps.title: Choose the site
buildSteps.detail: Surveys measure depth, currents, salinity, nutrient levels, seabed type and access to a harbour; permits are obtained for a defined sea area.

buildSteps.title: Design the mooring
buildSteps.detail: Engineers size anchors, line strengths and buoyancy for the worst storm the site can expect, and lay out the grow-lines in a grid.

buildSteps.title: Install the farm
buildSteps.detail: Anchors are set on the seabed and the grid of lines and floats is tensioned into position.

buildSteps.title: Seed the lines
buildSteps.detail: In a hatchery, kelp spores settle onto twine; that twine is wound around the grow-lines, and shellfish seed is filled into cages or nets. The farm is stocked in autumn as water cools.

buildSteps.title: Grow through the winter
buildSteps.detail: Kelp takes up nitrogen and phosphorus from the water and grows fastest in cold, nutrient-rich months; lines are checked, cleaned of fouling and adjusted for buoyancy.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and tend
buildSteps.detail: Divers or cameras inspect lines, cages and moorings; damaged gear is repaired and shellfish are thinned and re-graded.

buildSteps.title: Harvest
buildSteps.detail: A workboat hauls each line aboard and strips or cuts the crop; shellfish are lifted in the same pass. Typically the seaweed is cut in late winter to early spring.

buildSteps.title: Process and restock
buildSteps.detail: Seaweed is blanched, dried, frozen or salted for food, feed or fertiliser; shellfish are graded and shipped cold. Lines are re-seeded for the next cycle.

prerequisites.why: the farm must survive storms without touching the seabed or breaking loose.
consistent juvenile supply, rather than wild spores, is what makes a farm plantable on schedule.
filter feeders are the second crop that makes the site profitable year-round.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, accurate site and current modelling
prerequisites.why: nutrient supply, wave loading and dispersal are hard to predict, and mistakes are expensive offshore.

prerequisites.tech: Drying, freezing and biorefining of seaweed
prerequisites.why: wet seaweed spoils within hours, so harvesting is limited by processing capacity.

pathway.milestone: small nearshore farms combining kelp and shellfish, mainly in sheltered coastal water
pathway.unlocks: proven biology, a real product range and practical know-how.

pathway.milestone: exposed, further-offshore farms with mechanised seeding and harvesting
pathway.unlocks: area far beyond what sheltered bays can offer.
shared anchors, vessels and export infrastructure, and a second income from the same sea area.

pathway.milestone: integrated marine biorefineries and low-methane feed additives from red seaweeds
pathway.unlocks: bulk markets for biomass that food sales alone cannot absorb.
